svg.text: K1b The turret: one hand on a rod from the ceiling
Disc turns in the ceiling, a rod slides and yaws through it, a welded elbow arm carries a magnet roll. All drives sit above, dry.
4 axes: disc D, Z, yaw Y, roll K · tool reach 185–535 mm from the axis
Z stroke 440 (arm z 1000–1440), 300 N, load cell ±10 g
yaw 40 Nm (110 N at the tool) · roll 0–150 rpm, 10 Nm
heaviest spare part: rod with arm, 6 kg
SECTION through the turret, in the plane of the arm
rod collar: scraper, flush ring, lantern;
lip seal on the dry side (seal 2)
coaming Ø 450, open seam 4 mm, air-swept;
disc Ø 420 on a slewing bearing (D, ±200°)
load cell between carriage and rod:
weighs every grip and every pour ±10 g

g.text: belt inside to the magnet can

svg.text: TOP VIEW: disc + yaw = a two-link arm
rod on a 175 mm circle (disc D) + arm 360 mm (yaw Y):
every point 185–535 mm from C, two elbow solutions;
tool heading tied to position: T0 or H1 turn the food instead.
K1: 3 turrets, 7.3 m of seam · K1b: 1 turret, 1.4 m

g.text: 1/4 Disc and yaw together: the disc (D) carries the rod round a 175 mm circle, the rod turns (Y) and swings the 360 mm arm — one two-link arm for the whole cell
2/4 Reaching round the turret: the tool point goes from the board on T0 to the front band and to the pans; it never needs food under the ceiling seam
3/4 Park and Z: the arm folds back over the well; the ball screw lowers the arm 440 mm, the load cell between carriage and rod weighs ±10 g
4/4 Roll (K): the core shaft and the belt in the arm turn the dry magnet rotor; the sleeve outside the welded can follows — it tilts, pours and flips the tool
